control-auto-complete-suggestion.summary: One entry in the `suggestions` of an [`auto_complete`](/docs/control-auto-complete). `key` is the text the user's typing is matched against, ignoring case, and `value` is the text the list shows; when one is missing the helper copies the other, and the first positional argument sets `key`. Give only `value:`, so that the user searches the text they see. After a pick, Android, Windows and Linux put the `value` in the field and iOS and macOS the `key`; `on_select` reports both in `event.selection`. A web app follows the device: in a browser on an iPhone, iPad or Mac it gets the iOS design.

control-autofill-group.summary: Groups the text fields of one form for the platform's autofill service, so that it can fill them together, for example a saved user name and password, and offer to save what the user typed. Give each field `autofill_hints`, such as `["username"]` or `["password"]`. `dispose_action` says what happens to the entered data when the group leaves the page: `"commit"` (default) offers to save it, `"cancel"` discards it. The group draws nothing itself.

control-cupertino-date-picker.summary: An iOS-style wheel for picking a date, a time, or both. Open it with `page.show_dialog(picker)`: on iOS and macOS the wheel slides up with Cancel and Done, and on Android, Windows and Linux the client shows the Material date picker dialog. A web app follows the device: in a browser on an iPhone, iPad or Mac it gets the iOS design. When the user confirms, `on_change` gets the picked moment in `event.data`, an ISO 8601 string in UTC. Pass `date_picker_mode: "dateAndTime"` for a date and a time: the 0.0.23 client does not recognize the `"date_and_time"` this helper sends by default and shows the date wheels only. In the next release the client reads `"date_and_time"` too, so by default the wheels show the date and the time on iOS and macOS. **Requires the next Ruflet release** (on `main`, not in 0.0.23). With 0.0.23 a picker added to the page shows nothing; drawing it in place with `page.add` (the wheel on iOS and macOS, a calendar elsewhere) needs the next release. **Requires the next Ruflet release** (on `main`, not in 0.0.23). `event.control.value` returns the same moment as `event.control.props["value"]`; with 0.0.23 it raises NoMethodError. **Requires the next Ruflet release** (on `main`, not in 0.0.23).

control-dropdown-option.summary: One option of a [`dropdown`](/docs/control-dropdown). `key` is what the dropdown stores in its `value` and reports in `on_select`, and `text` is what the user sees; either defaults to the other, and the first positional argument sets `key`. `content` shows a control in the menu instead of `text`. `leading_icon`, `trailing_icon` and `style` apply on Android, Windows and Linux only: on iOS and macOS the options wheel shows each option's `content` or `text`. A web app follows the device: in a browser on an iPhone, iPad or Mac it gets the iOS design. A `disabled` option cannot be picked. On iOS and macOS the wheel dims it and Done stays off while the wheel rests on it; the 0.0.23 client still lets the user pick it there. **Requires the next Ruflet release** (on `main`, not in 0.0.23).

control-option.summary: Flet's dropdown option, kept for code written for `dropdown_m2`. In a [`dropdown`](/docs/control-dropdown) it works like a [`dropdown_option`](/docs/control-dropdown-option): `key` is what the dropdown stores and reports, `text` what the user sees, and `content` replaces `text` in the menu. It has its own `on_click`, which only iOS and macOS send, after the dropdown's `on_select`, so handle `on_select` on the dropdown. A web app follows the device: in a browser on an iPhone, iPad or Mac it gets the iOS design. `alignment` and `text_style` have no effect.

control-popup-menu-item.summary: One entry in a [`popup_menu_button`](/docs/control-popup-menu-button) menu, with text, an icon, or both. Set `checked` for a check mark. The client does not change it, so keep the state yourself and update `checked` in `on_click`: `event.data` is `true` or `nil`, never `false`, and the 0.0.23 client on iOS and macOS sends none. Leave out both text and icon for a divider. Icons, check marks and dividers show on Android, web, Windows and Linux only: on iOS and macOS the menu shows each item's text and nothing else, and an item without text draws an error box.
example: popup_menu_item("Name", icon: "sort_by_alpha", on_click: ->(_event) { page.update(sort, value: "Sorted by name") }),
popup_menu_item("Date", icon: "event", on_click: ->(_event) { page.update(sort, value: "Sorted by date") }),

control-segment.summary: One option of a [`segmented_button`](/docs/control-segmented-button). `value` is required, and is what the button reports in `selected` and `on_change`; `label` and `icon` are what the user sees.
example: segment("grid", label: "Grid", icon: icon("grid_view"), tooltip: "Show a grid"),
segment("map", label: "Map", icon: icon("map"), disabled: true)
